newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end up on improved sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end up on improved sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended up on Friday, the third consecutive day of gains, on improved market sentiment, traders said.
The most active September 1997 contract ended at 3,349 yuan ($404) per tonne, rising four yuan. It opened at an intraday low of 3,340, hitting a high of 3,355 yuan.
March did not trade, May rose 20 yuan to 3,320, July 34 to 3,405, November nine to 3,359 and the January 1998 contract nine to 3,369.
Combined volume fell to 26,200 tonnes from 29,200.
Most contracts opened lower but buying at low levels pushed prices up to end near or at their intraday highs.
Traders said gains in spot soybean prices on the world market and domestic producing regions support futures contract gains.
"Price rises on the spot market boosted confidence of long position holders on the futures market, resulting in active buying today," one trader said.
"Firm spot prices will continue to support the futures prices in the short term," he said.
